Structure as data/telescopes/hst.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; telescope{key, name, imaging_record, recommended_preset, explorer_inputs, params, foci[], pupil{summary, explorer_inputs, segment_centres_STPSF, segment_vertices_STPSF, strut_polygons_STPSF, tpupil_format, params}, not_found, conflicts, notes}. _meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short verbatim quote from the saved document; pdf_page = page of the saved PDF where the quote was found. derived = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). check 'ocr' = found in tesseract OCR of the figure; check 'figure' = FIGURE READ-OFF, read visually from a saved image (not machine-checkable).
_meta.coordinates: V1 = boresight (origin at the primary vertex, MC23), +V3 away from the sunshield, +V2 completes a right-handed set (JDC). Pupil coordinates: entrance pupil seen from the sky looking in, x = +V2, y = +V3, metres (STPSF convention; STD, STU).
_meta.design_vs_asbuilt: G06 (2006) is the pre-launch design (focal-surface position); MC23 (2023) and R23 (2023) the as-built/commissioned telescope; the STPSF pupil (2010 area budget, Ball drawings) is the model STScI uses for PSFs today.
_meta.quote_check: 102 quoted entries checked against the saved files: 90 matched in the text layer (pdftotext -layout and -raw per page; HTML tag-stripped and raw; .py/.rst raw text), 9 in tesseract OCR of figure renders, 3 FIGURE READ-OFF entries checked visually (labels on a photograph or image without readable text), 0 failing; plus 8 short quotations inside notes checked the same way.
_meta.quote_normalisation: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, en/em dashes, minus, multiplication sign (to x), division slash, tilde operator, soft hyphen and non-breaking/thin spaces normalised; whitespace collapsed; a quote also passes with PDF line-end hyphenation removed or kept as a hyphen, or with all whitespace removed (superscripts such as 'm2'); ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows are quoted as whitespace-separated cells.

telescope.name: James Webb Space Telescope -- Optical Telescope Element (OTE)
telescope.imaging_record: data/imaging/space_wide.json#jwst_nircam (telescope rows: D, eps, F, EFL, field)
telescope.recommended_preset: Three-mirror anastigmat with a flat fine steering mirror (FSM). Primary: 18 hexagonal beryllium segments, 1.32 m flat-to-flat, 7 mm gaps, two rings (6 A inside, 6 B + 6 C outside) around an empty hexagonal centre filled by the aft optics; circumscribed 6.6035 m in the STPSF pupil model (6.64 m in MC23), entrance pupil 6.6 m, inscribed 5.4733 m, area-equivalent 5.7 m; RoC 15879.7 mm, conic -0.9967 (f = 7.94 m, f/1.20 DERIVED). Segments are flat-side-up in the V2/V3 entrance pupil (edges perpendicular to V3, corners along V2); the outline is rotated 30 deg (corners toward +/-V3). Secondary: convex, 0.738 m, RoC 1778.9 mm, conic -1.6598, 7.169 m in front of the primary, on a deployable tripod whose three struts cross the pupil: one along +V3 (0.119 m wide in the model) and two at 30 deg either side of -V3 (0.122 m), all to r = 3.30 m. The secondary lies inside the central hole, so there is no circular obscuration. Collecting area 25.44 m^2 measured (25.4 m^2 JDox; 26.3 m^2 polished). Foci: an intermediate Cassegrain focus at the AOS entrance (EFL 59.4 m, f/9 DERIVED, 2 reflections), then tertiary (728 x 517 mm, behind the primary vertex) and FSM (172.5 mm, at the exit pupil) to the f/20 telescope focus (EFL 131.4 m, 1.570"/mm DERIVED, ~18' x 9' field, 4 reflections) on a curved focal surface ~1.96 m behind the primary vertex, shared by NIRCam, NIRSpec, MIRI and FGS/NIRISS through pick-off mirrors.

exit_pupil.derived: DERIVED (approximate, along V1 only, ignoring the off-axis fold): 1047.8 - (-1960) = 3008 mm from the FSM to the focal surface; exit-pupil diameter ~ 3008 / 20 = 150 mm (FSM physical size 172.5 mm, MC23 Table 2).

pupil.summary: Entrance pupil = the 18-segment primary (the aperture stop for most modes), seen from the sky with x = +V2, y = +V3: segments flat-side-up (edges perpendicular to V3), corners along V2; outline corners toward +/-V3; hexagonal central hole 1.335 m flat-to-flat / 1.537 m corner-to-corner (same orientation as the segments), inside which the 0.738 m secondary hides; three struts: +V3 (0.1189 m, with two bumps for the mid-boom hinge and magnetic dampers) and two lower struts at azimuth 150 and 210 deg from +V3 (0.1224 m), each from the centre to r = 3.30 m. Geometric clear area of the STPSF model 25.78 m^2 (measured 25.44 m^2). Diffraction: six bright spikes at 60 deg plus a fainter horizontal pair from the +V3 strut.

explorer_inputs.frame: entrance pupil seen from the sky looking in: x = +V2 (right), y = +V3 (up), metres
explorer_inputs.rings: inner 6 (A1-A6, r = 1.3235 m); outer 12 (B1-B6 at r = 2.6347 m on the outline corners, C1-C6 at r = 2.2859 m mid-side); empty centre
explorer_inputs.segment_orientation: flat sides up: edges perpendicular to V3 at top and bottom, corners along +/-V2
explorer_inputs.outline_orientation: rotated 30 deg to the segments: corners (B segments) toward +/-V3 and +/-30 deg from +/-V2; serrated flat sides centred on the C segments (+/-V2, +/-60 deg)

central_hole.shape: hexagon, same orientation as the segments

explorer_inputs.secondary_obscuration: none beyond the hole (0.738 m secondary inside it)
explorer_inputs.diffraction_spikes: 6 bright at 60 deg intervals (segment and outline edges) + 2 fainter horizontal (along V2) from the +V3 strut (R23)

outline.quote: The primary mirror dimensions and the tiling configuration with 18 hexagonal-shaped segments to form a tricontagon.

struts.value: 3 struts meeting at the pupil centre: one along +V3 (to r = 3.30 m, crossing A1 and B1 along their centre lines), two at 30 deg either side of -V3 (azimuth 150 and 210 deg from +V3, i.e. -60 and -120 deg from +V2; to r = 3.30 m, along the A3/A4 and A4/A5 gaps and across C3 and C4). Widths in the model: +V3 strut 0.1189 m; lower struts 0.1224 m; bumps on the +V3 strut 0.1652 m wide (r = 2.146-2.365 m) and 0.1396 m wide (r = 2.483-2.544 m)

alternatives.value: one vertical strut -> two horizontal spikes
alternatives.quote: six stronger diffraction spikes at 60 degree intervals created by the segment and aperture edges, plus two ... fainter horizontal spikes created by the vertical secondary mirror support.

alternatives.value: strut seen in pupil images next to C3 (bottom right)
alternatives.quote: The large C3 segment event, which had the largest wavefront effect, can be seen next to the secondary mirror support strut (bottom right).

struts.note: Strut widths and positions are known only from the STPSF pupil model; no paper found states them. Attachment: MC23 says the tripod joins the primary centre section; in the pupil model all three struts run from the centre to r = 3.30 m: the +V3 strut ends at the outer edge of B1 (3.2797 m), the lower struts pass the outer corners of C3 and C4 (3.036 m) and end outside the aperture.
struts.derived: DERIVED (STC): strut1 axis direction -60.00 deg from +V2 (azimuth 150.00 deg from +V3), width 0.12243 m (perpendicular distance between its long edges), far end (1.6500, -2.8579) m, r = 3.3000 m; strut2 mirror image (-120 deg, azimuth 210 deg); strut3 x = +/-0.059435 m (width 0.11887 m), y = 0 to 3.30 m. The lower struts are parallel to segment edges (edge directions 0, 60, 120 deg), so their diffraction spikes fall on the six segment spikes; only the +V3 strut adds a pair (horizontal, along V2), as R23 describes. Area over segments: strut1 0.270, strut2 0.270, strut3 0.310, bumps 0.011 m^2; total 0.862 m^2.

secondary_obscuration.value: none beyond the central hole: the 0.738 m secondary lies inside the 1.335 m hexagonal hole, and the pupil model has no circular obscuration (only segments and struts)

alternatives.value: only the struts obscure the polished area
alternatives.quote: but the secondary mirror support struts obscure a small portion.
This class has no wavefront errors, it's just the pupil geometry including the segments

secondary_obscuration.note: A secondary-mirror baffle is not mentioned in any source found.
secondary_obscuration.derived: DERIVED: 0.738 m < hole flat-to-flat 1.335 m (inscribed circle of the hole), so the secondary's shadow falls in the hole. eps for a circular-obscuration explorer model: 0.20 (hole flat-to-flat / 6.6 m), 0.21 (equal-area hole / 6.6 m); the secondary alone 0.112.

other_obscurations.value: telescope: none beyond segments, gaps, hole and struts; instrument-specific pupil masks downstream: NIRISS CLEARP (pupil alignment reference), NIRSpec grating stop (8.41 x 7.91 m projected), coronagraph Lyot stops and the AMI mask
other_obscurations.quote: Note that long wavelength filters (>2.5 microns) are used with a pupil obscuration which includes the pupil alignment reference fixture. This is called the "CLEARP" pupil.

alternatives.quote: a rectangular pupil mask 8.41x7.91 m as projected onto the primary is added to the optical system at the pupil plane after the MSA.
NIRISS imaging PSFs at wavelengths ≥ 2.7 µm have stronger diffraction spikes due to additional pupil obscuration from the CLEARP pupil wheel position which must be used with those filters.

not_found: Strut widths, positions and attachment points in any JWST paper or JDox page: the only numbers are the STPSF pupil-model polygons (0.1189 m +V3 strut, 0.1224 m lower struts, 3.30 m long). Lightsey et al. 2012 (Opt. Eng. 51, 011003) and 2014 (SPIE 9143), cited by JDox for the OTE design, are not open access and were not obtained.
A written statement of the segment orientation in V2/V3 ('flat sides up'): taken from the STPSF vertex lists and the JDox Figure 1 photograph (visual), which agree.
A secondary-mirror baffle (none mentioned; the secondary sits inside the central hole).
A published plate scale at the telescope focus and at the Cassegrain (intermediate) focus: DERIVED only (1.5697 and 3.472 arcsec/mm).

The V1 position of the Cassegrain focus (DERIVED ~+1.39 to +1.40 m) and a post-launch V1 position and radius of curvature of the curved ISIM focal surface (G06 gives ~196 cm behind the vertex, 2006 design).
The V2/V3 position of the OTE field centre relative to the boresight in text; G06 Fig. 33 gives only axis labels (-9.1 to +9.1' in V2; -5.7 to +3.4' in V3, zero point not stated).
Segment corner-to-corner size in words (DERIVED 1.524 m from 1.32 m; STPSF 1.517 m).
conflicts: Circumscribed diameter: 6.64 m (MC23 Sec. 3.1) vs 6.6 m (MC23 Sec. 1; G06 Fig. 32 'PM diameter = 6.6 m (circumscribed circle)') vs 6.603464 m (STPSF, projected outer corners of the B segments) vs 6605.2 mm (MC23 Table 2 'Phys. Size'). MC23 also calls 6.6 m the entrance-pupil diameter.
Outline flat-to-flat: 6.575 m (MC23 text) vs '6.6 meters flat to flat' (MC23 Fig. 4 and G06 Fig. 34 labels) vs 6.559 m (STPSF projected, DERIVED).
Segment size: 1.32 m flat-to-flat (MC23, G06) vs '~1.4 m in diameter' (JDT) vs STPSF projected polygons 1.296-1.314 m flat-to-flat, 1.503-1.518 m corner-to-corner, and JWST_SEGMENT_RADIUS = 1.517/2.
Gaps: nominal 7 mm (MC23) vs 7.6-7.7 mm between the STPSF polygons (DERIVED).

Area: 25.44 m^2 measured (MC23 Table 1 and Sec. 5.4; R23) vs 25.4 m^2 (JDT) vs 25 m^2 (G06 design; requirement > 25 m^2) vs 25.78 m^2 from the STPSF polygons (DERIVED); polished area 26.3 m^2 (JDT) vs 26.64 m^2 (STPSF segments, DERIVED).
Secondary support: 'a tripod that consists of four composite tubes' (MC23) vs a 'tripod' (G06, JDT) and three strut polygons (STPSF).
Cassegrain-focus position (DERIVED only): V1 = +1402 mm from the EFL ratio vs +1389 mm from the paraxial mirror equation with the tabulated radii (table rounding).
notes: Pupil frame used throughout: entrance pupil seen from the sky looking in (STPSF convention, 'consistent with the JWST WSS'), x = +V2 to the right, y = +V3 up, metres. In this frame segment A1 and B1 lie on +V3, C2 on +V2, A4 and B4 on -V3. The +V3 strut is the one with the deployment hinge (STO). On the sky / exit pupil the picture is mirrored (STD).

Reflections: 2 to the Cassegrain (intermediate) focus (PM, SM); 4 to the telescope focal surface (PM, SM, TM, FSM); each instrument then starts with its own pick-off mirror(s) near the focal surface (MC23: 'one or more pickoff mirrors near the telescope’s focal surface').

Light path along V1 (MC23 Table 2, mm): PM vertex 0 -> SM +7169.0 -> Cassegrain focus ~+1395 (DERIVED) at the AOS entrance -> tertiary -796.3 (behind the PM vertex) -> FSM +1047.8 (exit pupil) -> curved focal surface ~-1960 (G06), behind the primary, where the ISIM pick-offs sit.

Explorer pupil: draw the 18 STPSF polygons (segment_vertices_STPSF) and subtract the three struts (strut_polygons_STPSF); a circular D/eps model is an approximation (D = 6.6 m, eps ~0.20 for the hexagonal hole).
The JDox Figure 1 photograph shows the secondary stowed: its strut positions are not the deployed geometry.
